Advanced: load from a file
From rift-table/ (needs lib/, key in riot-key.txt): run the commands below, then paste the game.json and hit Load.
riot-timeline-to-rift.mjs
Key at developer.riotgames.com into riot-key.txt, then:
node riot-timeline-to-rift.mjs --riot-id "You#TAG" --region americas --list — see your last 20 games
node riot-timeline-to-rift.mjs --riot-id "You#TAG" --region americas --out game.json — newest game
... --index 3 --out game.json — the 4th-newest instead

What this model knows — and doesn't

Modelled: team & lane gold, XP/level leads, turret and inhibitor state, dragon stacks / Soul / Elder, Baron & Herald, live-vs-dead players with time-scaled respawns, vision, a coarse per-lane wave state (crash / push / even) that feeds lane priority and a Tempo term, and a champion layer — every champion carries ratings for dueling, splitpushing, teamfighting, pick threat, mobility, range, frontline and scaling. Those ratings scale with each player's own gold and level lead, so a 10/1 Yasuo reads as able to win a 1v2 that a coinflip Yasuo can't, while an immobile ADC alone is still a free kill.

Not modelled: exact minion counts and bounce timing, ability match-ups and cooldowns, item actives and summoner spells, individual mechanics and outplay potential, and off-meta role assignments. The wave control is a 5-point estimate you set by hand, not a minion simulation. Champion ratings are broad archetype estimates, not tier-list precision. Treat a flagged "good" call as the higher-percentage choice, not a guarantee.

Your own games: load one from the panel above — type your Riot ID and pick a game, or paste a file the bundled script produces. It reconstructs per-minute frames (champions, positions, gold, objectives, deaths) from the Riot match timeline, so you can scrub to any minute and move pieces to explore what you could have done differently.
